full_judgment:
2. The property in dispute consists of a homestead land 11 acres in area upon which stood a tin-shed and a kitchen, bearing Plot No. 273 appertaining to khatian No. 326 of mouza Kaoraid under PS Sreepur which the applicant Abdul Baten purchased on 13.6.70 for a consideration of Tk. 2000.00. Abdul Baten sold the homestead to the petitioner Rahima Begum by a registered Kabala dated 5.4.74 for a consideration of Taka 10, 000'00. On 10.7.76 he filed an application under section 4 of the said Ordinance before the authorised Officer, that is local Circle Officer (Rev), praying for restoration of the homestead on the allegation of the transfer having been made during the period of economic distress for reasons of such distress. Rahima Begum appeared and filed a written objection denying Abdul Baten's allegations. Two witnesses namely Nirod Chand Saha identifier of the Kabala dated 5.4.74 and one Abdur Rahim Fakir were examined on behalf of Abdul Baten and six witnesses including the scribe of the kabala were examined on behalf of the other side. Neither the parties nor Rahima Begum's husband examined themselves. It however appears that the authorised officer did not record the deposition of the witnesses but merely noted in the order sheets the substance of the statements made by the witnesses on behalf of the respective parties. He rejected the application holding that the transfer could not come within the mischief of the said Ordinance by reason of the fact that it was not made for reasons of economic distress but for purchase of land elsewhere. 

 6. Section 3(2) provides "For the purpose of this Ordinance, transfer of agricultural land within the period of economic distress shall be deemed to have been made for reasons of such economic distress if the transferor or the members of his family do not in the aggregate own, after the transfer, more than three acres of such land. From this provision the only yardstick for determination of existence of economic distress is the quantum of agricultural land left with the transferor and the members of his family not exceeding 3 acres. The question as to for what purpose the transfer had been made is, in view of such clear provision of law, absolutely irrelevant, although however the learned Munsif has found in favour of existence of economic distress on some other grounds. The opposite parties case is that after the transfer he and other members of his family were left with only 1.01½ acres of agricultural lands as recorded in the khatian No. 815 of the case mouza the khatian with the record. On the other hand, the petitioner's case is that the vendor was left with more than three acres of agricultural lands as recorded in the khatian Nos. 158 and 142 and 173 of the case mouza. The total area of lands recorded in these three khatians as filed in the case is 13.07 acres owned by 14 co-sharers in each khatian. Therein the shares of individual holders are not separately mentioned nor the petitioner has disclosed the vendor's shares in these khatians and as such on normal calculation not even 1 acre of land falls in share of the transferor. As a matter of fact in the affidavit-in-reply the petitioner could not deny the opposite party's assertion in this regard in his counter affidavit. It is, therefore, clear that the petitioner has failed to show that the vendor was after the transfer left with more than three acres of agricultural lands. Although this aspect of the issue has escaped the notice of the learned Munsif, his finding has ultimately been correct that the transfer was made for reasons of economic distress.
